title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: an elliptic curve E over an algebraically closed field k. The text says the only essential hypothesis is that the base has residual characteristics ≠ 2, and that everything works over an arbitrary base S, compatibly with base change.

Step 1, the 2-torsion set. (1) J = ₂E(k)^*, the set of the three nonzero points of order 2. Over a base S, J is a finite étale scheme of degree 3.

Step 2, the quotient line. (2)–(3) The quotient E/(±id) is a projective line that depends only on J. Concretely, Σ_J = P(V_J), where V_J = ker(k^J --sum--> k) is 2-dimensional. Σ_J carries a canonical étale divisor D_J of degree 3, given by the three coordinate hyperplanes cut on V_J. This is a coordinate-free Legendre picture: the three branch points other than the origin are canonically labelled by J, so no ordering is chosen and S_3 = Aut(J) acts naturally.

Step 3, the equivalence of groupoids. Giving E is equivalent to giving:
- J;
- a point t in Σ_J^* = Σ_J − D_J, the image of 0_E;
- a line T (namely T_{E,0}) with an isomorphism T^{⊗2} ≅ T_{Σ,t}.
The isomorphism is the canonical second-order differential of the double cover E → Σ at the ramification point over t.

Why this works: the previous page shows that, once the monodromy class ξ is fixed, double covers totally ramified at t form a groupoid equivalent to pairs (line, square root of T_{X,t}). Here ξ is canonical, being ramified at all four points of D_J + t. So the moduli stack of elliptic curves over Z[1/2] becomes the stack of triples (J, t, T, iso). Equivalently, it is the S_3-quotient of the λ-line (P^1 minus 3 points), together with a μ_2-gerbe of square roots of T_{Σ,t}. The automorphism −1 of T corresponds to [−1] on E.

Step 4, the tangent bundle. (6) There is a canonical isomorphism T_Σ ≅ O_Σ(2)(ω). Here ω = ω(J) is the μ_2-torsor of the two circular orders (orientations) of J, and L(ω) = L ∧^{±1} ω. This is the Euler-sequence identity T_{P(V)} ≅ O(2) ⊗ det V, together with det V_J ≅ det k^J = k twisted by the sign torsor of J.

Where this leads (next page): T_{Σ,t} ≅ O_t(2) ⊗ ω is not canonically a square. So T ⊗ O_t(−1) is a square root of the orientation torsor, i.e. a μ_4-torsor Q (a 'combinatorial square') lifting ω through μ_4 → μ_2. The page is thus setting up an explicit, choice-free description of the stack of elliptic curves in characteristic ≠ 2:
- the λ-line modulo S_3;
- with the μ_2-gerbe given as the Bockstein of the sign torsor for 1 → μ_2 → μ_4 → μ_2 → 1;
- in effect a description via the order-12 group S_3 ×_{±1} μ_4.
errors: No mathematical error found. (2) labels E/(±1) as 'J-marked', but it carries four marked points: D_J and t. Only the three points of D_J are labelled by J; t is extra data, as (4) makes clear.

Over a general base S one must also check that the monodromy class ξ exists globally. The previous page's equivalence presupposes a fixed ξ. Here ξ is forced (nontrivial at all four branch points), so this is fine, but it is left implicit.
In (6), whether one gets det V or det V^* depends on the P(V) convention (lines versus hyperplanes). This is harmless, since μ_2-torsors are self-dual.

ideas.what: Canonical, ordering-free Legendre model: E/±1 ≅ P(ker(k^J → k)) with divisor D_J labelled by the nonzero 2-torsion J, and S_3 = Aut J acting
ideas.modern_name: Legendre form / moduli of elliptic curves with level-2 structure M(2), modulo S_3 = GL_2(F_2)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Legendre and Jacobi (classical); scheme-theoretic: Igusa, Deligne–Rapoport, Katz–Mazur

ideas.what: Equivalence of groupoids, over any base with 2 invertible: elliptic curves ↔ (degree-3 étale J, section t of Σ_J − D_J, line T with T^2 ≅ T_{Σ,t})
ideas.modern_name: Description of M_{1,1}[1/2] as a μ_2-gerbe (square root of the tangent line at the branch point) over the rigidified stack [(P^1 − 3 pts)/S_3]; stacks of cyclic covers
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in Deligne–Rapoport and Katz–Mazur; cyclic-cover stacks: Arsie–Vistoli (2004); Legendre/S_3 presentation used e.g. by Antieau–Meier (Brauer group of M_{1,1})

ideas.what: Canonical isomorphism T_{P(V_J)} ≅ O(2) ⊗ ω(J), with ω(J) the orientation (circular-order) torsor of the 3-element set J
ideas.modern_name: Euler sequence: T_{P(V)} ≅ O(2) ⊗ det V; det of a permutation representation equals the sign character
ideas.where_published: EGA-style generalities on P(V) (the explicit twist by orientation torsor is unsure)

ideas.what: Plan, carried out on the next page, to resolve the square-root ambiguity by twisting O_t(1) with a μ_4-torsor ('carré') whose diagonals give ω
ideas.modern_name: Gerbe class as Bockstein of the sign torsor under 1→μ_2→μ_4→μ_2→1; presentation via the group S_3 ×_{±1} μ_4 (order 12)
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure; related computations appear in work on Pic/Br of M_{1,1} (Mumford, Fulton–Olsson, Antieau–Meier)

missed.claim: The page and its sequel give a fully canonical description of the stack of elliptic curves over Z[1/2], with no ordering of 2-torsion and no coordinates. It consists of the λ-line attached intrinsically to a 3-element étale set, plus a μ_2-gerbe identified through T_Σ ≅ O(2)(ω) with the Bockstein of the orientation torsor (a μ_4 'square' lifting the circular orders). This packages the extension S_3 ×_{μ_2} μ_4 that governs the twist. Literature computations of Pic and Br of M_{1,1}[1/2] via the Legendre family use equivalent ingredients, but this intrinsic 'orientation torsor / combinatorial square' formulation is not standard as far as I know.
missed.quote: T_Σ ≃ O_Σ(2)(ω) où ω = ω(J) est l'un des deux ordres circulaires sur J
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives a choice-free, base-change-compatible presentation of M_{1,1}[1/2]. That is useful for explicit Picard and Brauer group computations, for TMF-type level-2 descent (M(2) with GL_2(F_2)-action), and for the combinatorial (dessin / Teichmüller-tower) viewpoint Grothendieck was developing in 1980–84. The degree of novelty is modest and uncertain.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is classical (Legendre model, double covers of P^1, the Euler sequence). What is distinctive is Grothendieck's intrinsic, coordinate-free packaging: J-marked P(V_J), the orientation torsor of the 3-element set, and the μ_4 'square' lifting it. This is a tidy description of the generic μ_2-gerbe on M_{1,1}[1/2], probably known in substance to specialists but not in this form.
